title: tensor-parallel: tuned collectives and comm/compute overlap for multi-GPU runtime
author: Asha Menon
description:
Motivation: Tensor-parallel workloads observed inconsistent throughput across multi-GPU nodes under stress testing. Root causes identified: suboptimal collective algorithm selection for medium-size tensor shards, NCCL fallback to slow ring algorithms under certain topologies, and synchronous scheduling that prevents overlap of NCCL communication with local kernel execution. In addition, KV cache sharding had contention on host->device transfers when continuous batching increased request fan-in. Goals: 1) Pick better collective algorithms and configure NCCL tunables per topology; 2) Introduce lightweight async launch points to overlap comm/compute; 3) Adjust KV cache sharding and prefetch pipeline to amortize host transfers under continuous batching.

Summary of changes: 1) runtime/tensor_parallel/collectives.cpp: Implemented topology-aware collective adapter that picks between nv_kernel-friendly trees, NCCL optimized rings, and hierarchical allreduce based on shard size and GPU interconnect graph. Added a small autotune table persisted per-machine to prefer algorithms that performed best during a short warmup phase. 2) runtime/nccl/config.cpp: Exposed NCCL parameters (NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE, NCCL_P2P_LEVEL, NCCL_COLL_ALGO_HINT) through runtime config with safe defaults. 3) runtime/scheduler/schedule_manager.cpp: Added a non-blocking schedule pass which inserts comm launch events and permits local kernel launches that are independent to proceed while the collective completes. This is gated behind a runtime config flag for conservative rollout. 4) runtime/kv_cache/sharding.cpp: Changed shard placement to prefer intra-node contiguous GPU slices and added async host->device prefetch for hot prefixes to reduce stalls when continuous batching creates simultaneous misses. 5) bench/bench_tp_nccl.py: New microbench harness to reproduce the exact tensor sizes and topologies we saw in production; added perf scripts to measure overlap efficiency. 6) ci/nccl-integration.yml: New nightly matrix job for NCCL smoke and regression tests across topologies (DGX, GCP-A2, AMAX nodes). 7) docs/perf/TP-NCCL.md: Added operational guidance and tuning knobs for Dedicated and Private deployments.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for the collective adapter logic and for the scheduler non-blocking pass. Integration tests added to CI matrix: initial runs failed intermittently due to a race in the async prefetch; fixed by adding a lightweight host-side completion callback and a single-inflight-per-shard backpressure token. Benchmarks on a 8x A100 node: end-to-end seq-latency reduced by 18-28% at batch sizes 1-8 for produced token paths; steady-state throughput increased 32-40% for our 16k token synthetic workload when tp shards were 4-8 GPUs. KV-cache miss latency reduced ~25% under high-concurrency continuous-batching scenarios. See bench/bench_tp_nccl.py output attached in commits.

Rollout plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag tp.experimental.overlap_comm_compute=false by default. Gradual rollout: enable on internal Dedicated cluster for 48h smoke; then enable in Canary pool (10% traffic) with monitoring dashboards (new panels added in docs/perf/TP-NCCL.md). If regressions appear, runtime will fallback to previous collective adapter and synchronous scheduler within 2 minutes via observed SLO breach automation.

Backward compatibility and risk: Default behavior unchanged. Exposed NCCL tunables are conservative and validated across our supported CUDA/NCCL matrix. The autotune cache is per-node and can be cleared by admin. Race conditions found during testing have been fixed; still flagged as medium risk because topology diversity in customer environments may vary. We added explicit telemetry (tp.collective.choice, tp.overlap_efficiency) to help triage.

Related work and context: This PR ties into ENG-10234 (tensor-parallel scheduling roadmap) and ENG-10277 (KV cache sharding improvements). It was developed in response to SUP-789 where a customer reported high variance in inference latency on 8-GPU nodes. Also referenced prior kernel fusion efforts in runtime/kernels/fusion_v2.

review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Left a few nits and asked for more comments on the autotune persistence format. Also requested a safety gate to disable autotune if metrics regress.

Asha Menon: Addressed Diego's comments; autotune format is a compact JSON with versioning and can be wiped via admin endpoint. Added tp.autotune.disable flag and a health check that reverts choices if end-to-end latency increases beyond threshold.
Lina Zhou: Noted potential memory pressure from prefetch tokens at extremely high concurrency; requested single-inflight-per-shard enforcement.
Asha Menon: Implemented single-inflight-per-shard token and added unit tests. Also added telemetry for token waits.
Maya Patel: Approved after CI stabilized and benchmarks were attached. Asked ops to schedule a canary window in Dedicated cluster.
CI Bot: Initial nccl-integration job failed on GCP-A2 due to missing driver on the runner; rerun passed after runner update.
release_notes: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel performance: topology-aware collectives, NCCL tuning knobs exposed, comm/compute overlap pass, and KV-cache prefetching. Defaults preserve existing behavior; gated rollout. Expected latency reductions (18-28%) and throughput gains (32-40%) in common workloads.
perf_benchmarks: Steady throughput: +32% to +40% on synthetic 16k token workload
KV-cache miss latency under continuous batching: -25%
